c.tagline: Russia's imperial capital of palaces, the Hermitage, and summer White Nights.

taxi.fareNote: Book through the Yandex Go app rather than hailing on the street, where unmetered private cabs overcharge. Foreign-issued Visa/Mastercard no longer work in Russia, so set the app to cash or pay the driver in rubles.

emergency.note: 112 is the unified emergency number reaching police, ambulance and fire; 101 is fire and 102 is police.

solo.f: Government travel advisory is the main factor (5/100)

hood_landmark.Petrogradsky: Peter and Paul Fortress, Saint Petersburg
hood_landmark.Vasileostrovsky: Strelka of Vasilyevsky Island, Saint Petersburg

avoid.reason: No true no-go zones for visitors; outlying dormitory districts like Kupchino and Devyatkino offer nothing to tourists and are best skipped late at night.
Pickpockets work Nevsky Prospekt, crowded metro stations and tourist sites, and overpriced-bar scams targeting foreigners occur at night.

hood_desc: The historic core spanning Nevsky Prospekt, the Hermitage/Winter Palace, St. Isaac's Cathedral and the Admiralty; grand imperial architecture and the city's must-see sights, ideal for first-timers who want everything walkable.

The central district around the eastern end of Nevsky Prospekt, Ploshchad Vosstaniya and Rubinstein Street's famous bar-and-restaurant strip; a lively base for dining and nightlife with the best transit links, next to Moskovsky Station.
An elegant residential island of Style Moderne (Art Nouveau) mansions, the Peter and Paul Fortress, the cruiser Aurora and leafy streets; calmer and more local while still close to the center.

Vasilyevsky Island, laid out on a grid of numbered 'lines,' home to the Strelka spit, the Rostral Columns, the university and the Kunstkamera; atmospheric river views and museums with a quieter, studenty feel.
A tranquil, romantic western quarter of canals, the Mariinsky Theatre, New Holland island and Dostoevsky-era streets; low-key and artistic, favored by those wanting local charm away from the crowds.
lodging: Four Seasons Hotel Lion Palace St. Petersburg

water.note: Improved treatment has cut historic giardia risk, but bottled water is still the safer bet for visitors.

transit.hours: The Metro runs from around 5:40 AM to midnight; trams, trolleybuses and buses run roughly 5:30 AM to midnight, with limited night bus routes.
transit.note: Saint Petersburg has one of the world's deepest metro systems (5 lines), complemented by an extensive tram, trolleybus and bus network. Note that most central Neva bridges are raised nightly (roughly 1:00-5:00 AM) during the navigation season, cutting the islands off from the mainland.
transit.pay: Pay with the rechargeable Podorozhnik card, a single-ride metro token (zheton), or contactless bank card at the turnstiles; a single ride is about 70-86 rubles. Foreign Visa/Mastercard no longer work, so buy a Podorozhnik with cash.

bus: Intercity coaches from the Obvodny Canal bus terminal
ferry: Marine Facade Passenger Port (Morskoy Vokzal) for cruise/ferry calls; river and canal boat services on the Neva
train: Moskovsky, Finlyandsky, Vitebsky, Baltiysky and Ladozhsky rail stations; Sapsan high-speed service to Moscow (~4 hrs)

transit.m: Bus 39 / 39E to Moskovskaya metro, then Metro Line 2 to the center (~45-60 min)
Yandex Go / taxi to the city center (30-40 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving about 10% for good service is appreciated. Some restaurants add a 10% service charge, so check the bill first.

landmarks: State Hermitage Museum & Winter Palace
The opulent former imperial residence turned one of the world's greatest art museums, its jade-green Baroque facade is unmistakably iconic.
Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood
A riot of colorful onion domes and mosaics built on the site of Tsar Alexander II's assassination, it is the city's most photographed building.
Peter and Paul Fortress
The birthplace of St. Petersburg, this star-shaped citadel with its golden-spired cathedral sits dramatically on the Neva River.
Peterhof Palace and Gardens
Peter the Great's 'Russian Versailles,' famed for its Grand Cascade of gilded fountains and statues overlooking the Gulf of Finland.
Catherine Palace (Tsarskoye Selo)
A dazzling blue-and-gold Rococo palace outside the city, home to the legendary reconstructed Amber Room.
St. Isaac's Cathedral
One of the largest domed cathedrals in the world, its massive gilded dome dominates the city skyline and offers sweeping panoramic views.
Palace Square
A vast, grand square anchored by the Alexander Column, framed by the Winter Palace and the sweeping arc of the General Staff Building.
Kazan Cathedral
Modeled on St. Peter's Basilica, its dramatic curved colonnade makes it one of Nevsky Prospekt's most striking landmarks.
Mariinsky Theatre
The historic home of Russian ballet and opera, an elegant 19th-century theater synonymous with world-class performing arts.
Nevsky Prospekt
The city's grand main avenue lined with palaces, cathedrals, and canals, offering some of St. Petersburg's most classic streetscapes.

train.note: Most of St Petersburg's international services have gone: the Allegro to Helsinki has been suspended since 2022 and the trains to Tallinn, Riga and Warsaw no longer run, leaving Belarus and Central Asia as the only cross-border routes. Domestically the Sapsan high-speed trains reach Moscow in about 4 hours from Moskovsky station, and sleepers serve Murmansk, Petrozavodsk and Kazan. Foreign cards generally do not work on the RZD site, so buy through an agent or at the station.

bus.note: Coaches are now the main overland link to the Baltics, leaving from the Baltiysky and Obvodny bus stations. Tallinn takes about 7 hours and Riga 11, with long waits at the Narva or Ivangorod border - check current crossing rules and your visa position carefully before travelling, as they have changed repeatedly. Domestic services reach Veliky Novgorod and Pskov.

ferry.note: There is no working international ferry from St Petersburg - the St Peter Line services to Helsinki, Stockholm and Tallinn have been suspended since 2022. Boats on the Neva and hydrofoils to Peterhof are summer sightseeing and day-trip services rather than transport out of the country.

half.name: Kronstadt
half.blurb: A naval fortress town about an hour away on Kotlin Island guards the sea approach to Saint Petersburg and has a large naval cathedral.

half.name: Pavlovsk
half.blurb: A palace and English-style landscape park about 45 minutes away was built for Tsar Paul I in the late 18th century.

half.name: Gatchina
half.blurb: A palace estate about an hour away combines a fortress-like residence with lakes and parkland once used by Tsar Paul I.

half.name: Oranienbaum
half.blurb: A palace complex about 50 minutes away escaped World War Two damage and retains original 18th-century interiors and pavilions.

full.name: Vyborg
full.blurb: A medieval castle town about two hours toward the Finnish border was long ruled by Sweden and Finland before becoming part of Russia.
